 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction

 Rahul Kumar Nayak Appellant(s)

entities.text: Rahul Kumar Nayak vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
VERSUS  THE STATE OF JHARKHAND Respondent(s)
 O R D E R Leave granted.

The appellant apprehends his arrest in connection with FIR No.50/2022 dated 03.06.2022,
registered at PS Kandra, District Saraikela for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420,
409, 418 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
Admittedly, the appellant has joined the investigation.
It is submitted that the matter has been resolved between the co-accused and the complainant.
Considering the above, we are inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the appellant is granted anticipatory bail on terms and conditions to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial court.
We make it clear that the appellant shall continue to cooperate with the investigation.
The appeal stands allowed, accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

.J. [M.M. SUNDRESH] ..J.
[SATISH CHANDRA SHARMA] NEW DELHI;
DECEMBER 05, 2025.
